title: Early-spark infra cribsheet — morning shift
content:
Purpose: ultra-compact cribsheet for my early-morning shift. Fast scan, hands-on tasks, and a few one-line reminders to prioritize things that reduce p99 latency and avoid token throttles.

Top-of-shift quick hits (3 min):
- Open the pool dashboard (infra/gpu-pools) and confirm active pools: squirrel, halley, aurora. If any are red, page SRE channel.
- Check queued jobs count: `kubectl get pods -n inference -l job=batch -o wide | wc -l` (aim < 40 queued).
- Read the high-level alert slack thread (ops-alerts) for any ongoing rollouts. If rollout in progress, expect higher queuing and KV pressure.

Priority checklist (order matters):
1) Prefix cache priming
   - Run small warmup traces for hot models (gpt-x-small, llama-2-13b-q8). Command (local): `scripts/warm_prefix.sh --model=gpt-x-small --tokens=128 --concurrency=4`
   - Verify prefix hit rate on console: expected > 60% for hosted traffic after priming.
2) Autoscaler sanity
   - Check dedicated pools autoscaler logs (date range last 6h). Confirm scale-down backoff not stuck.
   - If a pool scaled to 0 unexpectedly, hold traffic and escalate.
3) Network egress flakiness smoke
   - Quick curl to edge LB from control plane: `curl -sS -D - https://edge-east.rw-infer/api/health` should return 200 within 150ms. Note any >500ms as candidate for region fallback.
4) Preemptible node handback
   - Scan for imminent preemptions in cloud console. For nodes with <10min, trigger `drain-and-warm` job for critical routes.

Capacity knobs and thresholds to watch:
- p50 token latency target: <= 45ms; p95: <= 180ms; if p95 > 220ms for >5m, flip model-route to cheaper variant.
- Pool utilization target: keep GPUs <= 78% sustained to avoid OOM spikes.
- KV cache eviction rate: if eviction_rate > 0.03/sec, investigate memory pressure on sequence-length heavy workloads.

Common fixes and one-liners (copy-paste):
- Restart a hung batch worker: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/batch-worker -n inference`
- Clear local KV cache on node (safe): `ssh node && systemctl stop kvcache && rm -rf /var/lib/kvcache/* && systemctl start kvcache`
- Force a small scale-up for pool "squirrel" (temporary): `infractl pool scale --name squirrel --gpus 6`

Notes for networking oddities:
- If only one region shows increased RTT, consider routing policy override to fallback region for latency-sensitive routes. Document override in ops-ttl channel.
- For intermittent SSL handshakes failing: check cert-rotation job logs and restart the envoy sidecar for affected pods.

Operational reminders (things I tend to forget):
- After running warmups, update the warmup-timestamp tag on the pool (console -> tags) so next shift knows when last primed.
- If I escalate to oncall SRE, include the exact pool id and a link to the warmup run logs.

Short-term experiments to try this week (notes):
- Try batching window 12ms -> 10ms for low-latency routes; measure cost delta over 24h.
- Prototype a tiny probe that issues a 4-token prompt to all hot endpoints every 30s to keep fast KV entries in working set.

Random scribbles (do later):
- Investigate why aurora pool shows sporadic CUDA mem fragmentation after nightly jobs. Suspect old driver on node group b-12.
- Add a health-check that detects prefix cache coldness and suggests priming automatically.

Hand-off summary (if I need to hand off mid-shift):
- Last thing done: primed gpt-x-small & llama-2-13b-q8 at 07:20; prefix-hit rates back to ~68%.
- Any open tickets: JIRA-OPS-1297 (node b-12 memory fragmentation).
- Suggested next steps: keep an eye on p95 for the next 30m, and if it rises > 200ms, revert the latest canary toggle.

End-of-shift quick checklist:
- Leave a short note in ops-bridge: what was primed, any anomalies, and which pools were scaled manually.
- Snapshot warmup metrics and attach to ticket if anomaly persists.

——
Personal TODO (micro):

(If this file still looks messy, it's because it is meant to be — one-page, action-first reference for chaos mornings.)
